western.temperament: Curious, quick-witted, talkative and adaptable; astrology reads Mercury as a restless mind hungry for new information. Older folklore also calls Gemini inconstant. The twins myth (Castor the mortal, Pollux the son of Zeus) gives the sign its doubleness.

chinese.temperament: Witty, intelligent, mischievous, a fast learner and crafty opportunist; 'masters of practical jokes' in popular zodiac writing.
chinese.element: Metal (fixed element); earthly branch Shen, ruling hours 3 to 5 pm
chinese.trine: Rat, Dragon, Monkey (the 'achievers' trine: ambition and quick thinking)
chinese.secret_friend: Snake (six harmonies pair, called a 'clever combination')
chinese.lucky: Sources disagree. China Highlights: numbers 4 and 9, colors white, blue and gold, flowers chrysanthemum and crape myrtle, directions north, northwest and west (unlucky colors red and pink). Wikipedia: numbers 1, 3, 4, 7, 8 and avoid 9; colors include white, blue and gold. Only 4, white, blue and gold appear in both.

symbolism.meaning: The name kea copies the bird's own call (written 'keee aaa'). A bird that announces itself by name: a good image for a Gemini voice.
The Waitaha people held the kea, with the kāhu (harrier) and ruru (morepork), to be kaitiaki, guardians of their people. The trickster is also a protector.

Hut stories of kea sliding down roofs before dawn, riding a knocked-over ski downhill, stealing nails and hiding them sorted by size, and a snow-dropping prank at one hut that later turned up at Arthur's Pass, 30 km away. Mischief that gets taught and passed on.

High-country sheep farming from the 1870s brought accusations against kea, a bounty, and an estimated 150,000 birds shot before full legal protection in 1986. The bird blamed for more than it did: a strong shadow image.
Voted New Zealand's Bird of the Year in 2017 (7,311 votes), 'known fondly for its cheekiness.' Loved for exactly the trait that once got it shot.

Sun Wukong of Journey to the West: stone-born, intelligent, 'naughty and impish,' who rebels when given a lowly post and causes the Havoc in Heaven. The cultural model for the clever, rule-testing Monkey.

'Clown of the mountains' / 'clown of the Southern Alps' nickname appears in search titles only; not verified on a reliable page. Generic 'kea spirit animal' meanings found online have no traditional basis.

fusion.temperament: Ours: Gemini's Air wants to know; Monkey Metal wants to handle. The Kea is the mind that learns through its hands. You tend to understand a thing once you have taken it apart, and you narrate what you find while you are still finding it. Both halves are yang and both are restless, so the Kea runs warm and fast, and boredom is its real enemy.
fusion.gifts: Ours: reading an unfamiliar system quickly; making hard problems feel like play (anchored by the play call that makes other kea play); teaching by showing, the way the snow-drop prank spread between huts; staying cheerful in thin, cold places where others give up.
fusion.shadow: Ours: touching what was fine, testing people the way you test latches, getting blamed for damage you only meant as interest (the bounty years are the image). Gemini's inconstancy plus the Monkey's opportunism can read as unreliable.
fusion.love: Ours: falls for the person who stays interesting. Courts with jokes and questions, needs a partner who enjoys being figured out and pokes back. Trust grows when the other person lets the Kea in on the workings of their life. Loses interest when everything is already known; does best with someone who keeps a little mystery and a lot of humor.
fusion.money: Ours, with the traditional Monkey link to trading and opportunism (s9): quick to spot a deal and quick to earn, also quick to spend on the next gadget or trip. Does well with a second person or an automatic rule holding the savings.
fusion.conflict: Ours: defuses with a joke first, argues with facts second, and can outtalk people without meaning to. Under real pressure the Kea flies off to another ridge rather than sitting in the cold. Growth is staying in the room long enough to finish the repair.

candidate_lines: You tend to understand a thing best once you have had it in pieces on the table.
There are times when you start explaining an idea before it is finished, and the explaining is how you finish it.
You often loosen a room before anyone agrees to be loosened, and people only notice later that they were laughing.
You tend to trust the people who let you poke at their plans and still like you afterward.
There are times when you leave with a crowd of friends instead of a map, and it goes better than the map would have.
You often get blamed for the mess you only came over to look at.

fact_audit.fact: The only alpine parrot; South Island mountains, beech forest and sub-alpine scrub, roughly 600 to 2,000 m
fact_audit.note: DOC calls it the world's only mountain parrot, endemic to the Southern Alps; ADW gives wooded valleys, southern beech and sub-alpine scrub at 600 to 2000 m.

fact_audit.fact: Long decurved upper bill used to dig roots and grubs, strip bark, pry into things
fact_audit.note: ADW confirms the decurved upper bill but not the listed uses. Te Ara says kea investigate with beaks, tongues and claws. Uses are plausible; need a source before keeping the exact list.

fact_audit.fact: Kea dismantle human belongings (wipers, seals, ski gear); researchers frame it as curiosity-driven, not food-motivated
fact_audit.note: First half OK: ADW says they investigate human belongings and destroy car accessories and ski lodge equipment, explained as opportunistic exploration. The 'rather than food-motivated' contrast is not in ADW, and Te Ara notes they open bins to find food. Soften to 'often with no food in sight' or cite a study.

fact_audit.fact: Play call broadcast to wild kea made them play more, emotional contagion
fact_audit.note: Schwing et al. 2017, Current Biology: birds hearing play calls played more and longer, some starting when no other bird was playing; first known non-mammal with an emotionally contagious call.

fact_audit.fact: Aggregations of 30 to 40 at rich feeding sites; dominance hierarchies not strictly linear (adult > young > juvenile > adult example)
fact_audit.note: ADW: aggregations of 30 to 40 at prime feeding grounds such as dumps; hierarchies 'not necessarily linear.' The circular example is the page's illustration, not a sourced observation; 'not strictly' should read 'not necessarily.' 'Family groups' not checked.

fact_audit.fact: Juveniles disperse and travel together in flocks for two to three years before settling
fact_audit.note: ADW states this almost word for word.

fact_audit.fact: Intro: crow-sized olive-green parrot, orange-red underwing, 'one of the most cognitively sophisticated birds studied in captivity'
fact_audit.note: Not checked against a fetched source this session. Underwing color is widely reported but the cognition superlative needs a citation (the page's PMC3110758 link may cover it; it could not be opened here).

fact_audit.fact: January or early February birthdays can belong to the Goat year; Monkey years 1992, 2004, 2016
fact_audit.note: Goat precedes Monkey in the cycle; years follow the 12-year pattern. Monkey hours 3 to 5 pm per Wikipedia.
